title: Rat Emoji 🐀 Meaning: Snitches, Gym Rats and Pet Rats
description: The 🐀 rat emoji can mean a snitch, a betrayer, a gym rat, a scrappy goblin mood or simply a pet rat. Here is how to read it and when it is an insult.
summary: The 🐀 rat emoji shows a full-bodied gray rat with a long tail. It is often an insult meaning a snitch, traitor or sneaky person, but it also covers gym rats and mall rats, chaotic snack-hoarding moods, city pests, pet rat owners and the Rat in the Chinese zodiac.
meaning: The sharpest meaning is betrayal. To rat someone out is to tell on them, and calling a person a rat means they snitched or switched sides. Sending 🐀 about someone in a group chat is a clear accusation. Sports fans use it for players who leave for a rival team, and crime dramas have made the word a fixture.

The word also attaches to devotion. A gym rat practically lives at the gym, a mall rat haunts the shopping center and a rink rat or library rat does the same elsewhere. In these uses 🐀 is affectionate, even proud, and it often appears next to the place in question.

Online, rats have picked up a scrappy, chaotic charm. People describe eating cheese at midnight, hoarding snacks or digging through the fridge in pajamas as rat behavior, and some embrace an unpolished rat era instead of a glamorous one. Rat girl summer became a TikTok phrase for exactly that mood.

Literal uses remain: pest control, city rats on subway tracks and the famous pizza-carrying rat clips from New York, plus pet rat owners who adore their clever, social animals. During Lunar New Year, 🐀 stands for the Rat, the first animal in the Chinese zodiac, associated with quick wits and resourcefulness.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Most often it accuses someone of snitching: who told the teacher, who leaked the surprise, who posted the screenshot. It can also be a playful self-label for gremlin habits like eating straight from the fridge. Tone depends heavily on whether it is pointed at someone or at oneself.

contexts.label: In sports and gaming
contexts.body: Fans call a player who leaves for a rival or a teammate who betrays the squad a rat. In games, it can describe someone who hides in corners or steals kills. Gym rats use it in workout check-ins as a badge of dedication.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: In the Chinese zodiac the Rat is the first of twelve animals and is associated with cleverness and resourcefulness. People born in Rat years use 🐀 for their sign, and it appears in Lunar New Year greetings when a Rat year comes around.

combos.meaning: Snitching and the rule against it; keep quiet.
Rat behavior: snacking, hoarding or chaotic eating.

Year of the Rat greetings for Lunar New Year.

confusedWith.difference: 🐁 is a small mouse with rounder ears and lighter build, usually cute or literal. 🐀 is larger and carries the snitch and traitor meanings. Calling someone a mouse suggests timid; calling them a rat suggests disloyal.
🐭 is a friendly cartoon mouse face, used for cute or shy energy. The rat is a realistic full body and rarely reads as sweet, except among pet owners.

avoid: Do not use it about real informants or witnesses, where the label can put someone at risk.
Avoid it in food business messages, since a rat image implies contamination.
design: A full side view of a gray or brown rat walking on all fours with a long, thin, hairless tail, pink ears and whiskers. Vendors draw it fairly realistically, which makes it look less cute than the cartoon mouse face. It does not take skin tone modifiers.

faqs.a: Usually a snitch or traitor, someone who told on others or switched sides. It can also mean a dedicated regular, as in gym rat, or describe chaotic, scrappy behavior in a joking way.

faqs.q: Is the rat emoji an insult?
faqs.a: Pointed at another person, yes. It accuses them of disloyalty or sneakiness. Used about oneself or a hobby, such as gym rat, it is lighthearted. Read who it is aimed at.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🐀 and 🐁?
faqs.a: 🐀 is a rat, larger with a long tail, and carries the snitch meaning. 🐁 is a mouse, smaller and usually neutral or cute. Both are full-body animals, unlike the 🐭 mouse face.

faqs.q: What does 🐀 mean for Chinese New Year?
faqs.a: It represents the Rat, the first sign of the Chinese zodiac. People use it to greet a Year of the Rat or to show they were born in one.
